topStories.headline: Staunton Stabbing Suspect Held Without Bond as ICE Detainer Puts Virginia's Sanctuary Policies in the Spotlight
topStories.dek: A fatal August stabbing on Orchard Avenue has escalated into a statewide fight over whether Virginia jails must honor federal immigration detainers.
topStories.body:
A 21-year-old woman is dead and another is recovering after a stabbing in the early hours of August 30 inside a home on the 300 block of Orchard Avenue in Staunton. Freddi Chigo Mil, 32, was arrested at the scene after Staunton Police responded to an open-line 911 call around 4 a.m. He faces charges of second-degree murder and aggravated malicious wounding and remains jailed without bond at Middle River Regional Jail.

Federal authorities identified Mil as a Mexican national who entered the country illegally. Immigration and Customs Enforcement lodged a detainer with the jail on the day of his arrest, asking Virginia officials to ensure he remains in custody so he can be transferred to federal immigration authorities if released from state custody. The Department of Homeland Security publicized the detainer in a September 15 statement, and the case drew renewed national attention as of October 1, 2026.

The case has reignited a dispute over Virginia's cooperation with ICE. Gov. Abigail Spanberger's administration has said the state continues to cooperate with federal law enforcement under specified legal circumstances and that her policies are intended to improve officer safety and public trust. The criminal case against Mil remains pending; he has not been convicted of the charges against him. ICE's detainer seeks to ensure federal immigration authorities can assume custody if he later becomes eligible for release.

topStories.headline: Police Chief Breaks Silence on Walmart Shooting; Staunton NAACP Demands More Answers
topStories.dek: Chief James Williams confirmed body-camera footage has been handed to state investigators but will not be released, while the local NAACP branch called the pace of public disclosure insufficient.
topStories.body:
Staunton Police Chief James Williams issued an updated public statement on September 29 regarding the fatal officer-involved shooting that occurred September 22 in the parking lot of the Walmart on Richmond Avenue — the first substantive statement from department leadership since the incident. An officer had responded to a 911 call from a citizen and made contact with Montique Treymayne Gaston, 39, of Portsmouth. An altercation followed during which the officer fired their weapon. Gaston was pronounced dead at the scene; the officer was not injured and has been placed on administrative leave.

Chief Williams confirmed the involved officer was wearing a body-worn camera that recorded the entire incident, and that footage has been turned over to the Virginia State Police, which is conducting an independent investigation at SPD's request. The footage will not be released while the probe is open. Williams said the department does not have all the facts and that it would be inappropriate to reach conclusions before all evidence is examined. He acknowledged the shooting's impact on Gaston's family and on the African American community specifically.

The Staunton Branch NAACP called for more transparency, stating that significant questions about what precipitated the encounter and the sequence of events leading to deadly force remain publicly unanswered. Branch President Nadia Ware said, as quoted by WAVY News: "Transparency is not the enemy of a fair investigation; it is essential to public confidence in one." The branch called for preservation of all potentially relevant evidence, including body-camera footage, 911 recordings, dispatch audio, and surveillance video from Walmart and nearby businesses. Future updates on the investigation are to come from Virginia State Police.

topStories.headline: Friends of the Library to Cut the Ribbon on Long-Awaited Outdoor Terrace October 9
topStories.dek: A years-in-the-making terrace renovation behind the Staunton Public Library — funded entirely by a private estate gift — reaches its final phase with a public grand-opening celebration Friday morning.
topStories.body:
The Friends of the Staunton Library will host a grand opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony for the Library Terrace Project on Friday, October 9, beginning at 10 a.m. at the Staunton Public Library, 1 Churchville Avenue. The event marks the completion of a multi-phase renovation of the library's backyard first presented to City Council in Winter 2024, when it received unanimous support.

The finished terrace includes tiered hardscape seating built into the existing hillside, a patio event space suited for library programs and small performances, a shade sail, improved lighting, and a new accessible pathway connecting the library building to the raised terrace area. Construction of the patio and walkway ran from May through July 2026, with the shade structure installed in late July and landscaping continuing through this fall.

The project was made possible entirely by an estate gift from Julia Kiessling, a former member of the Friends of the Staunton Library board. The Friends pledged to plant a replacement tree for every one removed during site preparation. The completed terrace is designed to function as an accessible community gathering space open for public enjoyment as well as library-hosted events.

moreNews.headline: State Resists Closure of Staunton Children's Psychiatric Hospital Despite Repeated Legislative Calls
moreNews.body: Virginia's nonpartisan research arm, the Joint Legislative Audit and Review Commission (JLARC), renewed its call in early September 2026 to close the Commonwealth Center for Children and Adolescents (CCCA) in Staunton — the state's only psychiatric hospital for minors. JLARC Director Hal Greer told the commission the body has no reason to believe conditions have improved significantly since the original 2023 report, and that staff continue to raise concerns about patient and employee safety. Despite those findings, the Spanberger administration is not moving toward closure: a spokesperson for the Virginia Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services told media outlets that the agency is "not currently pursuing closure." The Augusta Free Press reported on the continuing standoff on September 28, 2026.

moreNews.headline: No School for Staunton City Students October 12–13 as First Quarter Ends
moreNews.body: The first nine weeks of the 2026–27 Staunton City Schools academic year concludes on Friday, October 9. Students will have no school on Monday, October 12 (teacher workday) and Tuesday, October 13 (parent conference day). The second quarter begins Wednesday, October 14, per the district's published academic calendar.
